title: Access and inspect work sites for pests

lessons.title: Gaining access to the work site
lessons.html:
Access starts before you arrive

Accessing a work site professionally and safely is the first practical skill of a pest management officer. Whether the site is a farmhouse, a 20-bin silo complex, a bakery or a game lodge, the officer must arrive prepared, be authorised and understand the site's rules and hazards.

Pre-visit checklist

  • Confirm the appointment, address, site contact name and phone number.
  • Review the job request and any previous service reports, trap data and site plans.
  • Confirm which areas must be inspected and whether special access is needed: roof spaces, silo tops, tunnels, production areas, locked stores.
  • Ask about site requirements: induction, visitor register, PPE, food safety rules, vehicle routes, permits for confined spaces or work at height.
  • Check that your registration card, company identification and relevant documents are with you.
  • Prepare and check inspection equipment and PPE.

On arrival

  1. Report to reception, security or the site manager and sign the visitor or contractor register.
  2. Complete the site induction. Note the emergency assembly point, alarms, first aid and fire equipment.
  3. Meet the site contact and confirm the scope of the inspection, areas you may enter and any restricted areas.
  4. Ask about current pest sightings, complaints, recent changes such as renovations, new stock or new equipment, and any recent pesticide or fumigant use.
  5. Agree how you will report urgent findings before you leave.

Site hazard awareness

Conduct a quick on-site risk assessment before inspecting each area. Typical hazards include moving vehicles and forklifts, conveyors and augers, open pits, grain engulfment, residual fumigant gas, heat in roof spaces, fragile ceilings and roof sheets, electrical installations, animals such as dogs or livestock, and biohazards in drains. Where entry to a silo, bin, tunnel or tank is required, confirm that a confined space permit, lockout and standby person are in place. If an area is unsafe, do not enter: record it as inaccessible and inform the client.

Professional conduct

Respect the client's property and operations. Wear a clean uniform, follow hygiene rules, avoid disturbing production, and keep the client informed of where you are working.

lessons.title: Carrying out the inspection
lessons.html:
A systematic route

Plan a route that covers every area without doubling back. A common approach is exterior perimeter first, then the building from roof or upper levels down, moving room by room in the same direction, ending with service areas such as refuse rooms and drains.

Exterior inspection

  • Walk the perimeter. Look for rodent burrows, runways in grass, droppings and gnawing.
  • Check vegetation touching buildings, which gives rodents and insects a bridge.
  • Inspect refuse areas, drains, standing water and grain spillage around intake pits and loading points.
  • Look for bird roosting and nesting on ledges, beams and silo tops.
  • Inspect doors, vents, pipe penetrations and gaps under roller doors for entry points.
  • Check timber structures and soil contact for termite mud tubes.

Interior inspection

  • Use a torch and mirror behind and under equipment, inside motor housings and in wall voids.
  • Check along wall-floor junctions where rodents run and insects hide.
  • Inspect stored product: sieve samples, check bag stacks for webbing, frass and holes.
  • Check ceilings and roof spaces for droppings, nests, damage to wiring and timber.
  • Service and read existing monitors: bait stations, insect light traps, pheromone traps and sticky monitors.

Recording as you go

Record findings at the location, not from memory later. For each finding note the location against the site plan, evidence type, pest if identified, activity level and photographs. Mark conducive conditions such as spillage, damaged proofing, leaks and clutter. Collect specimens in labelled vials for identification where needed.

Closing the visit

  1. Leave all areas as you found them, close doors and hatches and replace ceiling panels.
  2. Brief the site contact on key findings and urgent risks.
  3. Agree next steps: written report, quotation or treatment schedule.
  4. Sign out of the site register.

Complete the written report promptly, stating areas inspected and those not accessible, findings and recommendations.

Key points

  • Prepare documents, equipment, PPE and site requirements before arriving.
  • Sign in, complete induction and confirm scope and restricted areas with the site contact.
  • Assess hazards before entering each area and never enter unsafe or unpermitted confined spaces.
  • Follow a systematic route, exterior first, and record findings at the location.
  • Brief the client before leaving and report inaccessible areas.
